subtopics.name: Predicting & Deducing the Type of Polymerisation

parts.problem_md:
Glycine and serine are amino acids with the systematic names 2-aminoethanoic acid and 2-amino-3-hydroxypropanoic acid respectively.

Draw the structural formulae of glycine and serine.
parts.solution_md:
The he structural formulae of glycine and serine are:

Glycine:

![Structural formula of glycine (2-aminoethanoic acid) showing an amino group (–NH₂) bonded to a CH₂ group bonded to a carboxylic acid group (–COOH)](assets/001-structural-formula-of-glycine-2-aminoethanoic-ac.png)

Serine:

![Structural formula of serine (2-amino-3-hydroxypropanoic acid) showing an amino group (–NH₂) and a hydroxymethyl group (–CH₂OH) on the central carbon, with a terminal carboxylic acid group (–COOH)](assets/002-structural-formula-of-serine-2-amino-3-hydroxypr.png)

**[2 marks]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> 1 mark for the correct structure of glycine
> 
> 1 mark for the correct structure of serine
> 
> Allow skeletal formulae

> **[exam-tip]**
> Glycine (2-aminoethanoic acid): based on ethanoic acid with one H on the CH<sub>3</sub> group replaced by –NH<sub>2</sub>, giving H<sub>2</sub>N–CH<sub>2</sub>–COOH.
> 
> Serine (2-amino-3-hydroxypropanoic acid): based on propanoic acid with one H on C-2 replaced by –NH<sub>2</sub> and one H on C-3 replaced by –OH, giving H<sub>2</sub>N–CH(CH<sub>2</sub>OH)–COOH.

parts.problem_md:
Serine exists as a pair of optical isomers. The three-dimensional structure of one optical isomer is shown in Fig. 3.2.

![Three-dimensional structure of one optical isomer of serine showing a chiral carbon with wedge-dash bonds connecting –NH₂, –CH₂OH, –COOH, and –H groups](assets/003-three-dimensional-structure-of-one-optical-isome.png)

**Fig. 3.2**

Draw the three-dimensional structure of the other optical isomer of serine.
parts.solution_md:
The three-dimensional structure of the other optical isomer of serine is:

![Three-dimensional structure of the other optical isomer of serine, the mirror image of Fig. 3.2 with wedge and dash bonds reversed around the chiral carbon](assets/004-three-dimensional-structure-of-the-other-optical.png)

**[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> 1 mark for the correct mirror image of Fig. 3.2 with all four groups retained and wedge-dash bonds reversed

> **[exam-tip]**
> The two optical isomers are non-superimposable mirror images of each other. The simplest approach is to reverse the wedge and dash bonds while keeping all four groups attached to the chiral carbon.

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

Glycine and serine are amino acids with the systematic names 2-aminoethanoic acid and 2-amino-3-hydroxypropanoic acid respectively.

Glycine and serine can react to form condensation polymers containing ester and amide linkages.

State the names of the functional groups that react to form:

i) an ester linkage

[1]

ii) an amide linkage

[1]
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> i) The functional groups that react to form an ester linkage are:
> 
> - Hydroxyl / –OH
> **AND**
> carboxylic acid / –COOH **[1 mark]**
> 
> ii) The functional groups that react to form an amide linkage are:
> 
> - Amine / amino / –NH₂
> **AND**
> carboxylic acid / –COOH **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> An ester linkage forms from a reaction between a hydroxyl group (–OH) and a carboxylic acid group (–COOH). Only serine has a hydroxyl group, so ester formation requires at least one serine monomer.
> 
> An amide linkage forms from a reaction between an amine group (–NH<sub>2</sub>) and a carboxylic acid group (–COOH). Both glycine and serine have these groups, so amide linkages can form between any combination of the two amino acids.

parts.problem_md:
Glycolic acid polymerises to form polyglycolic acid (PGA). The structure of glycolic acid is shown in Fig. 1.1.

![Displayed formula of glycolic acid showing a hydroxyl group (–OH) bonded to a CH₂ group, bonded to a carboxylic acid group (–COOH)](assets/005-displayed-formula-of-glycolic-acid-showing-a-hyd.png)

**Fig. 1.1**

State the systematic name of glycolic acid.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> The systematic name of glycolic acid is:
> 
> - 2-hydroxyethanoic acid
> **OR**
> hydroxyethanoic acid **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Glycolic acid (HOCH<sub>2</sub>COOH) contains two functional groups: a carboxylic acid group (–COOH) and a hydroxyl group (–OH).
> 
> The name is built from: hydroxy- (for –OH) + ethan- (two carbons) + -oic acid (for –COOH) = 2-hydroxyethanoic acid. The locant 2 is not required as the –OH can only be on C-2.

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

Glycolic acid polymerises to form polyglycolic acid (PGA). The structure of glycolic acid is shown in Fig. 1.1.

Glycolic acid (HOCH₂COOH) contains two functional groups: a carboxylic acid group (–COOH) and a hydroxyl group (–OH).

State the type of polymerisation involved in the formation of PGA and state the name of the functional group formed between the monomers.

type of polymerisation: ..............................

functional group: ..............................
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> The type of polymerisation and functional group formed are:
> 
> - Type of polymerisation: condensation **[1 mark]**
> - Functional group: ester **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Glycolic acid contains both a carboxylic acid group (–COOH) and a hydroxyl group (–OH). When these groups from two monomers react, they form an ester linkage and release water, which is condensation polymerisation.

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

Glycolic acid polymerises to form polyglycolic acid (PGA). The structure of glycolic acid is shown in Fig. 1.1.

![Displayed formula of glycolic acid showing a hydroxyl group (–OH) bonded to a CH₂ group, bonded to a carboxylic acid group (–COOH)](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/03/glyolic-acid.png)

Draw a section of the PGA polymer chain showing two repeat units. The ester linkages must be shown fully displayed.

Label one repeat unit on your diagram.
parts.solution_md:
A  section of the PGA polymer chain showing two repeat units is:

![Structural diagram of two repeat units of PGA (polyglycolic acid) showing ester linkages fully displayed and continuation bonds at each end, with one repeat unit labelled](assets/006-structural-diagram-of-two-repeat-units-of-pga-po.png)

**[2 marks]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> 1 mark for a diagram with continuation bonds **AND** a minimum of two monomers
> 
> 1 mark for a correct repeat unit **OR** a correct ester linkage
> 
> 1 mark for the rest of the diagram fully correct

> **[exam-tip]**
> PGA is a polyester: the carboxylic acid group of one glycolic acid monomer reacts with the hydroxyl group of another, releasing water (condensation polymerisation) and forming an ester linkage.
> 
> A common mistake is to omit the continuation bonds at each end of the drawn chain, which are required for full marks.

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

State the type of polymerisation involved in the formation of PGA and state the name of the functional group formed between the monomers.

type of polymerisation: ..............................

functional group: ..............................

The type of polymerisation and functional group formed are:

- Type of polymerisation: condensation
- Functional group: ester

State whether PGA is biodegradable. Explain your answer.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Whether PGA is biodegradable and why:
> 
> - PGA is biodegradable **[1 mark]**
> - The ester linkage / ester bond can be hydrolysed / undergoes hydrolysis **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> PGA is a polyester. Ester bonds can be broken down by hydrolysis (reaction with water or enzymes), making PGA biodegradable.
> 
> This contrasts with addition polymers such as poly(ethene), which contain only C–C and C–H bonds in the backbone. These cannot be hydrolysed and are therefore non-biodegradable.

parts.problem_md:
Fig. 2.1 shows the structure of dehydroalanine.

![Displayed formula of dehydroalanine showing an amino group (–NH₂), a carboxylic acid group (–COOH), and an alkene group (C=CH₂)](assets/007-displayed-formula-of-dehydroalanine-showing-an-a.png)

**Fig. 2.1**

State the name of the functional group in dehydroalanine that is not present in most naturally occurring amino acids.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> The functional group not present in most naturally occurring amino acids is:
> 
> - Alkene / carbon–carbon double bond / C=C **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Amino acids contain two common functional groups: an amino group (–NH<sub>2</sub>) and a carboxylic acid group (–COOH).
> 
> Dehydroalanine also contains an alkene group (C=CH<sub>2</sub>), which is not found in most naturally occurring amino acids.

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

Fig. 2.1 shows the structure of dehydroalanine.

Displayed formula of dehydroalanine showing an amino group (–NH₂), a carboxylic acid group (–COOH), and an alkene group (C=CH₂)

Fig. 2.1

Dehydroalanine can undergo addition polymerisation.

Draw one repeat unit of the addition polymer formed by dehydroalanine.
parts.solution_md:
One repeat unit of the addition polymer formed by dehydroalanine is:

![Structural diagram showing one repeat unit of the addition polymer formed from dehydroalanine, with the C=CH₂ double bond opened and continuation bonds shown, retaining –NH₂ and –COOH groups](assets/008-structural-diagram-showing-one-repeat-unit-of-th.png)

**[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> 1 mark for a correct repeat unit with continuation bonds shown

> **[exam-tip]**
> In addition polymerisation, the alkene (C=CH<sub>2</sub>) double bond opens. The repeat unit retains the –NH<sub>2</sub> and –COOH groups.
> 
> Continuation bonds must be shown at each end of the repeat unit.

parts.problem_md:
The catalytic hydrogenation of dehydroalanine produces alanine, CH<sub>3</sub>CH(NH<sub>2</sub>)COOH.

Draw a section of the condensation polymer formed by alanine showing two repeat units. The peptide bond must be shown fully displayed.
parts.solution_md:
A section of the condensation polymer formed by alanine showing two repeat units is:

![Structural diagram showing two repeat units of the condensation polymer of alanine with peptide bonds (–CO–NH–) fully displayed and continuation bonds shown](assets/009-structural-diagram-showing-two-repeat-units-of-t.png)

**[2 marks]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> 1 mark for a diagram with continuation bonds **AND** a minimum of two monomers **AND** the amide / peptide linkage is correct
> 
> 1 mark for the rest of the diagram fully correct

> **[exam-tip]**
> Alanine undergoes condensation polymerisation: the carboxylic acid group (–COOH) of one monomer reacts with the amino group (–NH<sub>2</sub>) of the next, releasing water and forming a peptide (amide) bond (–CO–NH–).
> 
> A common mistake is to omit the continuation bonds at each end of the drawn chain.
